parts.label: (a)
hints: Hint 1: Think about what happens at a single point in space when two or more waves arrive there at the same time.
Hint 2: Remember that displacement is a vector, so think about how you combine the individual displacements to get the total displacement at that point.
parts.proper_answer: When two or more waves meet at a point, the resultant displacement is the vector sum of the individual displacements of the waves.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Picture waves overlapping**
Imagine two ripples crossing each other on water. At any instant where they overlap, the water is moved by both waves at once. Superposition is all about what happens at that meeting point.

Step 2: **Add displacements to get the result**
At the meeting point, you simply add the displacements. If both try to lift the medium up, you get a bigger lift. If one lifts and one pushes down, they partly cancel. In symbols, $$x_{total} = x_1 + x_2 + ...$$ where $x$ is displacement, keeping the sign for direction.

parts.label: (b)(i)
hints: Hint 1: A stationary wave needs two identical waves travelling in opposite directions - think about where the second, backward-travelling wave could come from.
parts.proper_answer: The metal plate reflects the incident microwaves back towards the transmitter to allow superposition with the forward wave to form a stationary wave.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What a stationary wave needs**
You get a stationary wave only when a forward wave and a backward wave of the same frequency and wavelength overlap and interfere. Here the transmitter only sends waves one way, toward the plate.

Step 2: **Role of the plate**
The metal plate acts as a reflector. It sends the microwaves straight back along the same line, so you now have two oppositely travelling waves in the same region that superpose to give nodes and antinodes.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Microwaves are part of the electromagnetic spectrum, so think about what speed they travel at in air.
Hint 2: Think about how wave speed, frequency and wavelength are linked, and rearrange to make frequency the subject.
Hint 3: Check your units carefully - you will first get frequency in Hz, then convert to GHz using $1 \text{ GHz} = 10^9 \text{ Hz}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify the wave speed**
All electromagnetic waves in air travel at essentially the speed of light, $$c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$$ The wavelength is given as $$\lambda = 0.040 \text{ m}$$

Step 2: **Use the wave equation**
Frequency, wavelength and speed are linked by $$c = f\lambda$$ Rearranged for frequency: $$f = \frac{c}{\lambda}$$ Substitute values: $$f = \frac{3.0 \times 10^8}{0.040} = 7.5 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}$$

Step 3: **Convert to GHz**
Since $$1 \text{ GHz} = 1 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}$$ $$f = \frac{7.5 \times 10^9}{10^9} = 7.5 \text{ GHz}$$

parts.label: (b)(iii)
hints: Hint 1: In a stationary wave, think about how far apart two neighbouring nodes (intensity minima) are in terms of wavelength $\lambda$.
Hint 2: For the count, think about how many half-wavelength intervals fit into 9.1 cm, and remember a maximum lies halfway between each pair of minima.
parts.proper_answer: Shortest distance between minima $= 0.020 \text{ m}$. Number of maxima in 9.1 cm $= 5$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Distance between minima**
An intensity minimum is a node where destructive superposition gives zero amplitude. Neighbouring nodes are separated by half a wavelength: $$d = \frac{\lambda}{2}$$ So $$d = \frac{0.040}{2} = 0.020 \text{ m}$$ This is the shortest move from one minimum to the next minimum.

Step 2: **Count the maxima in 9.1 cm**
An intensity maximum is an antinode, which sits exactly halfway between two nodes. So as you move, minima and maxima alternate every $0.020 \text{ m}$ for minima and every $0.010 \text{ m}$ shift for min to max. Convert the travel: $$9.1 \text{ cm} = 0.091 \text{ m}$$ Number of node spacings covered: $$\frac{0.091}{0.020} = 4.55$$ That means you pass through 4 full node-to-node intervals plus part of a fifth. Each full interval contains one maximum, plus one more maximum in the partial interval, giving $$4 + 1 = 5$$ maxima detected.
